$comment: The http_request_cache_settings ruleset for assets.latam-tools.com.br.
Applied by tools/apply-cloudflare.mjs, which PUTs this whole array to the
phase entrypoint. That endpoint replaces the ruleset wholesale, so this file
is the complete desired state: a rule deleted here is deleted in Cloudflare on
the next apply. There is no state file and no drift to reconcile.
EVERY rule must test http.host. This zone also serves latam-market, short,
simulador-latam-ro and latam-social; a rule without the host check would
silently change caching for all of them.
Order matters — Cloudflare evaluates top to bottom and the last match wins for
a given setting, so the bypass rule comes first.

rules.description: ragassets: never cache the help page or the health check
rules.expression: (http.host eq "assets.latam-tools.com.br" and (http.request.uri.path eq "/" or http.request.uri.path eq "/healthz"))

rules.description: ragassets: renders — the URLs Cloudflare would not cache on its own
$comment: This rule is the reason the migration is worth anything. Cloudflare Free
decides what to cache by file extension, and /image?job=1002&action=0 has
none — so the most expensive responses on the site are precisely the ones
it would skip. On the old Worker route the Worker ran in front of the cache
and renders were never stored at all (no CF-Cache-Status header in
production, re-rendered every request).
The query string IS the identity of a render, so it must be in the cache
key in full. Note api.ETagFor hashes the query order-independently while
this key does not: ?job=1&action=0 and ?action=0&job=1 are two edge entries
holding identical bytes. Extra misses, never wrong bytes.
Most of these carry a file extension and would cache anyway. The rule
exists for the query-keyed /effect/* endpoints, and so the whole policy is
stated in one place rather than half-implicit in Cloudflare's extension
list.
respect_origin keeps the split the Go server already makes: immutable for
assets, max-age=300 must-revalidate for /raw. Do not flatten these into a
fixed TTL — three sibling projects poll /raw/items.json on every client
update and depend on revalidating.
rules.expression: (http.host eq "assets.latam-tools.com.br" and (starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/icons/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/illust/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/effects/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/effect/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/maps/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/bgm/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/raw/")))
